subject: Re: Dedicated staged rollouts — audit log event schema + retention language for enterprise security reviews
body:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 9:12 AM PST
Subject: Dedicated staged rollouts — audit log event schema + retention language for enterprise security reviews

Hey Marcus —

We’re getting pulled into 2 enterprise security reviews for Dedicated staged rollouts (reserved pools). Both are specifically asking for:

1) A clear audit event taxonomy for rollout actions (create/update/approve/abort/auto-hold/rollback)
2) Retention guarantees and whether logs are immutable / exportable
3) A paragraph we can paste into security questionnaires (SOC2 change mgmt controls)

Can you review the draft event schema and the retention language below and suggest changes? We’re aiming to send to Northbridge by end of week.

Draft retention language (current):
- “Redwood retains audit logs for 90 days and supports export upon request.”

Draft events (high level):
- rollout.plan.create
- rollout.plan.update
- rollout.stage.approve
- rollout.stage.abort
- rollout.stage.hold.auto (gate failure / missing metrics)

Thanks,
Marissa

—

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 11:03 AM PST
Subject: Re: Dedicated staged rollouts — audit log event schema + retention language for enterprise security reviews

A few changes needed before we put this in front of an enterprise security team:

Retention:
- 90 days is going to be a red flag (and it conflicts with what we’ve said elsewhere for platform audit logs). We should align to “>= 1 year” for SOC 2 expectations.
- Proposed: “Audit logs are retained for 400 days in Redwood-managed storage by default. Customers can export audit logs to their SIEM/storage for longer retention.”
  - 400 days gives us cushion over 365 and matches how we talk about other security logs.
  - For Dedicated/Private, we should be careful: if they’re VPC/on-prem, retention is configurable and may be customer-managed. For this thread (Dedicated, Redwood-operated reserved pools), we can make a clean statement.

Event taxonomy:
- We should separate “plan CRUD” from “execution state changes.” Also include stage advancement events and rollback events.
- Recommend we add:
  - rollout.plan.publish (or rollout.plan.activate) — when it becomes the active plan for a pool
  - rollout.stage.advance.requested (manual or automatic)
  - rollout.stage.advance.completed
  - rollout.stage.rollback.requested
  - rollout.stage.rollback.completed
  - rollout.gate.evaluation.failed (include gate_id + measurement window)

Fields:
- Most reviewers will ask “what is captured?” We should standardize on:
  - timestamp (RFC3339)
  - actor_type (user/service)
  - actor_id (Redwood user id) + actor_email (if user)
  - actor_roles (at time of action)
  - tenant_id
  - pool_id
  - rollout_plan_id + plan_version
  - stage_id
  - action
  - request_id / trace_id
  - source_ip + user_agent (if action via Console/API)
  - reason (optional freeform, but we need guidance not to put secrets/PHI)

Immutability:
- Phrase as “append-only” / “tamper-evident controls” rather than “immutable” unless we’re prepared to defend specifics.

If you want, I can draft the security-questionnaire paragraph too.

Marcus
Security Lead, Redwood Inference

—

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 1:26 PM PST
Subject: Re: Dedicated staged rollouts — audit log event schema + retention language for enterprise security reviews

+1 to Marcus.

Two additional notes from a “what will procurement/security latch onto” perspective:

1) Be explicit that approvals are recorded with who/when/what changed (plan_version). Reviewers are looking for change management controls, not just activity logs.
2) Don’t promise export “upon request.” We should say “available via API and export pipeline” (even if beta is limited) so it’s framed as a product capability.

If we’re not GA on export for rollouts yet, we can say:
- “Audit events are available in the Redwood Console and via Audit Log API; SIEM export is available for enterprise accounts (GA for core audit logs; rollout events in beta).”

Neha

Subject: Re: Dedicated staged rollouts — audit log event schema + retention language for enterprise security reviews

Context: Northbridge’s ticket (SUP-3981) explicitly asks for “audit trail of rollout approvals” + “log retention >= 12 months” + “export to Splunk.”

They’ll accept “Console + API now, Splunk export by [date]” but they need it written down.

Rachel

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 16, 2025 at 10:18 AM PST
Subject: Draft language + attachment for Northbridge (audit logging / retention / change mgmt)

Draft language you can paste into questionnaires (feel free to lightly edit for tone):

---
Change management & audit logging (Dedicated staged rollouts)
Redwood Inference records audit events for administrative actions that change rollout configuration or state, including creation and updates to rollout plans, publishing/activation of a plan to a dedicated pool, stage approvals, aborts, stage advancement, automatic holds triggered by gate failures (e.g., latency/error/queue depth thresholds) or missing telemetry, and rollback requests/completions. Audit events include the acting identity (user or service), timestamp, tenant and pool identifiers, the rollout plan identifier and version, and relevant stage/gate identifiers. Approvals are logged with approver identity and the plan/stage version approved.

Retention & access
Audit logs are retained for 400 days in Redwood-managed storage by default for hosted/dedicated deployments. Audit events are append-only and protected by access controls and operational safeguards. Audit logs are available in the Redwood Console and via Audit Log API; enterprise customers may also enable export to their SIEM/storage for extended retention.
---

Attachment: Dedicated_Rollout_Audit_Events_v0.3.pdf

Open question for you/PM: do we want to name specific gate metrics (p95 latency, 5xx rate, timeout rate, GPU utilization, queue depth), or keep it generic? Security teams sometimes want specifics, but it can create a maintenance burden.

Marcus

—

From: Sana Iqbal <sana.iqbal@northbridgebank.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Evan Roemer <evan.roemer@northbridgebank.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jan 17, 2025 at 2:41 PM PST
Subject: Re: Audit trail + retention for staged rollouts (Dedicated)

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for the draft. A couple of clarification questions for our SOC2 + internal change management controls:

1) When you say “append-only,” do administrators at Redwood have the ability to modify/delete audit events?
2) Do you capture the “before” and “after” values when a rollout plan is updated (or at least a diff)?
3) For retention, can you confirm the minimum is 400 days and whether this applies per-tenant? We need to document that logs are not co-mingled across tenants.
4) For export: is Splunk supported directly, or would we be pulling via API and forwarding ourselves?

If you can answer in writing, we can close out this section of our review.

Regards,
Sana Iqbal
Information Security Risk — Third Party
Northbridge Bank

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sana Iqbal <sana.iqbal@northbridgebank.com>
Cc: Evan Roemer <evan.roemer@northbridgebank.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Jan 20, 2025 at 9:37 AM PST
Subject: Re: Audit trail + retention for staged rollouts (Dedicated)

Hi Sana,

Answers inline:

1) “Append-only” / modification & deletion
Audit events are generated server-side and written as append-only records. Access to audit log storage is tightly restricted. Routine administrative workflows do not support modifying or deleting individual events. We also monitor for anomalies in audit event ingestion.

2) Before/after values (or diff)
For plan updates, the audit event includes identifiers (rollout_plan_id, plan_version) and references the updated plan version. In the Console/API, operators can retrieve the full plan version history. For certain fields we also include a summarized change descriptor (e.g., “stage_weights updated,” “gate_threshold updated”). We generally avoid embedding full “before/after” payloads directly in the audit event to reduce risk of sensitive data appearing in logs.

3) Retention and tenant isolation
For Dedicated deployments operated by Redwood, audit logs are retained for a minimum of 400 days by default. Audit events are scoped with tenant_id and access is enforced by RBAC; customers only have access to their own tenant’s audit logs. Dedicated pools are isolated per tenant; audit events include the dedicated pool identifier to support auditing at the pool level.

4) Export / Splunk
Today, audit logs are available via the Console and Audit Log API. For SIEM, customers typically pull via API and forward to Splunk (HEC) or another SIEM. Direct managed Splunk integration can be provided for select enterprise accounts; we can confirm scope/timeline with your account team based on your preferred ingestion method.

If you’d like, we can also provide an example event (redacted) showing an approval action and the included fields.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Security Lead, Redwood Inference

Marcus,

This is helpful. A redacted example event for “stage approval” would be great, especially showing how you record approver identity and the plan/stage version.

Also, please confirm whether “reason” is required or optional, and whether Redwood provides guidance to avoid secrets/credentials in free text.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Audit trail + retention for staged rollouts (Dedicated)

Sana,

Sharing a redacted example of a stage approval event below (format shown as JSON for readability; this is representative):

Event: rollout.stage.approve
- timestamp: 2025-01-21T16:12:09Z
- actor_type: user
- actor_id: usr_8f3…
- actor_email: approver@redwoodinference.com
- actor_roles: ["dedicated_ops", "rollout_approver"]
- tenant_id: tnt_nb_…
- pool_id: pool_dedicated_nb_prod_01
- rollout_plan_id: rpl_2c1…
- plan_version: 7
- stage_id: stage_2
- action: approve
- request_id: req_91b…
- source_ip: (redacted)
- user_agent: RedwoodConsole/1.214.0
- reason: "Approved after 30m stable p95 + 0.1% error rate" (optional)

On “reason”: it is optional (not required to approve). In the Console, we include guidance text to avoid entering secrets, credentials, or sensitive customer data in free-text fields. We also have automated checks in some surfaces to prevent obviously sensitive patterns.

If you need anything else for your review, please let Rachel know and we’ll respond quickly.

Best,
Marcus
